body:
This connector now matches the react-instantsearch API, it exposes `indices` as an array and a `refine` function to update the query 👍

I've build a simple example with https://selectize.github.io/selectize.js/ which integrates well.

* [x] documentation
* [x] tests

This PR replaces #2651

> Rebased on feat/2.8 & changed pull request base branch.

Inside the stories the select component keep the items in memory. It means that the more we search the longer is the list (see below). We can use the `clearOptions()` to remove all options before each new render. 

Note that the autocomplete widget is always tied with the main search. For example if we want to only target an different index than the main one we can't. We will need to use another instance and sync them together. The use case I'm thinking of is the e-commerce demo with the suggestions. 

![untitled](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6513513/40077204-30e85e38-5881-11e8-94e0-4701789eebd0.gif)

> Inside the stories the select component keep the items in memory. It means that the more we search the longer is the list (see below). We can use the clearOptions() to remove all options before each a new render.

Nice catch, internally selectize keeps in memory options added and re-do a search into them.

> Note that the autocomplete widget is always tied with the main search. For example if we want to only target an different index than the main one we can't. We will need to use another instance and sync them together. The use case I'm thinking of is the e-commerce demo with the suggestions.

Yes it's true, good point, as a solution we can also provide another option to do not use the "main index" and so the user has to specify at least one index in the options. What do you think?

> Yes it's true, good point, as a solution we can also provide another option to do not use the "main index" and so the user has to specify at least one index in the options. What do you think?

I don't think it will solve the issue because even with only a different index the query will still be set on the main helper. For the suggestions example it means that the "suggested" hits and the "regular" hits will always be in sync.

> I don't think it will solve the issue because even with only a different index the query will still be set on the main helper. For the suggestions example it means that the "suggested" hits and the "regular" hits will always be in sync.

If I sum we have 3 cases (with my thoughts):
 - If it's an independant search. Having independant searches seems fine.
 - If if you want to sync the main results and the autocomplete results but with different indices, the idea to have an option for "not the main index" seems to solve it
 - If you have the main index + others and everything is synced, it's the default case

Did I miss something @iam4x @samouss ?

>  - If it's an independant search. Having independant searches seems fine.

Yes it's fine.

> - If if you want to sync the main results and the autocomplete results but with different indices, the idea to have an option for "not the main index" seems to solve it

We can also go in the other directions, do not assume that the autocomplete will be on the main index. WDYT? I'm still fine with the current proposal, it's just that I didn't think about it before.

> - If you have the main index + others and everything is synced, it's the default case

Yes indeed, depends on your answers on the question above.
